speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; let's start by asking, did these symptoms come on suddenly or did they develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Pancoast syndrome.

Given your history of smoking, weight loss, and progressive right arm weakness with sensory changes, I suspect a tumor in the lung apex compressing the brachial plexus. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, MRI_Brachial_Plexus.
